span-indexofanyexcept.title: Find the first non-matching value with IndexOfAnyExcept
span-indexofanyexcept.short: Search a span for the first element outside an excluded set
span-indexofanyexcept.summary: IndexOfAnyExcept returns the position of the first element that is not one of the specified values.
span-indexofanyexcept.why: Negative searches such as skipping a whitespace prefix can be expressed without a manual loop.
span-indexofanyexcept.tips: When the searched value set is larger and reused, consider a reusable SearchValues<T> instance.

collectionsmarshal-asspan-list.title: Access List<T> storage directly with CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan
collectionsmarshal-asspan-list.short: View list elements as a span without copying
collectionsmarshal-asspan-list.summary: CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan creates a Span<T> over the internal storage of a List<T>.
collectionsmarshal-asspan-list.why: Measured internal hot paths can reduce indexer overhead and temporary copying.
collectionsmarshal-asspan-list.tips: Changing the list size can invalidate the span, so keep this API inside tightly controlled low-level code.

jsonnode-deepequals.title: Compare JSON structures with JsonNode.DeepEquals
jsonnode-deepequals.short: Compare JSON values by content instead of object identity
jsonnode-deepequals.summary: JsonNode.DeepEquals compares two JSON nodes according to their represented content and structure.
jsonnode-deepequals.why: DOM objects can be checked for JSON equality without relying on reference equality.
jsonnode-deepequals.tips: This is structural JSON comparison, not a byte-for-byte comparison of the original textual representation.

environment-processpath.title: Get the executable path with Environment.ProcessPath
environment-processpath.short: Ask for the executable backing the current process
environment-processpath.summary: Environment.ProcessPath returns the path of the executable associated with the current process when available.
environment-processpath.why: Diagnostics and relaunch logic can obtain the executable location without confusing it with the working directory.
environment-processpath.tips: The value can be null, and AppContext.BaseDirectory may be the better base for application data files.

regex-enumeratesplits-span.title: Enumerate regex split ranges with Regex.EnumerateSplits
regex-enumeratesplits-span.short: Split with a regex without allocating every substring
regex-enumeratesplits-span.summary: EnumerateSplits uses regex delimiters and enumerates the ranges of the resulting parts in the original input.
regex-enumeratesplits-span.why: Code that consumes each part immediately can avoid allocating a new string for every split segment.
regex-enumeratesplits-span.tips: The results are ranges into the source; process them as spans and materialize strings only when they must outlive the input.

timespan-parseexact.title: Require an exact duration format with TimeSpan.ParseExact
timespan-parseexact.short: Accept only the duration syntax your format defines
timespan-parseexact.summary: ParseExact converts text to TimeSpan only when it matches the requested format and culture.
timespan-parseexact.why: Configuration and wire formats can define an unambiguous accepted duration syntax.
timespan-parseexact.tips: Use TryParseExact when invalid user input is an expected outcome rather than an exceptional condition.

memorymarshal-asbytes.title: View value spans as bytes with MemoryMarshal.AsBytes
memorymarshal-asbytes.short: Expose contiguous value storage as bytes without copying
memorymarshal-asbytes.summary: MemoryMarshal.AsBytes reinterprets a span of non-reference values as a byte span over the same memory.
memorymarshal-asbytes.why: Binary and low-level code can inspect existing storage without allocating an intermediate byte array.
memorymarshal-asbytes.tips: In-memory representation depends on layout and endianness; prefer explicit encoding for persistent formats.

utf8jsonreader-skip.title: Skip unwanted JSON values with Utf8JsonReader.Skip
utf8jsonreader-skip.short: Advance past an entire object or array you do not need
utf8jsonreader-skip.summary: Skip advances past the current JSON value without requiring the caller to process every nested token.
utf8jsonreader-skip.why: Streaming parsers can ignore unknown or irrelevant compound properties while reading only needed fields.
utf8jsonreader-skip.tips: Understand the reader's current token and test how Skip interacts with the following Read call.

wait-handle-waitasync.title: Await a WaitHandle with WaitOneAsync
wait-handle-waitasync.short: Bridge OS-style wait handles into asynchronous code
wait-handle-waitasync.summary: WaitOneAsync asynchronously waits for a WaitHandle signal while supporting timeout and cancellation.
wait-handle-waitasync.why: Interop boundaries can avoid occupying a thread with a synchronous WaitOne call.
wait-handle-waitasync.tips: For new purely managed async designs, prefer primitives such as SemaphoreSlim that are async-aware by design.

convert-trytohexstring.title: Write hexadecimal output into an existing buffer with Convert.TryToHexString
convert-trytohexstring.short: Avoid allocating a new hexadecimal string
convert-trytohexstring.summary: TryToHexString writes the hexadecimal representation of bytes into a caller-provided character span.
convert-trytohexstring.why: High-frequency conversion can reuse output storage instead of allocating a new string each time.
convert-trytohexstring.tips: ToHexString is simpler for ordinary use; choose the Try API when buffer reuse is measurably useful.
